basics.name: Yimin Zhao
basics.label: PhD Candidate in Biostatistics
basics.summary: PhD candidate at the University of Washington working on trustworthy medical AI, including evaluation of LLM and agentic systems for factuality, evidence grounding, and knowledge currency. Lead PanCanBench and contribute to Agents’ Last Exam and Terminal-Bench Science. Interned at Microsoft on Copilot Studio, developing a new Copilot SDK retrieval tool and a self-evolving agent framework. Over five years of experience modeling high-dimensional biological sequencing data, with publications in Nature Communications and Bioinformatics.

highlights: Advisors: Jeff Leek, Mike Wu, Kevin Lin

work.name: Microsoft
work.position: PhD Intern, Applied Science and Research Team
highlights: Developed a self-evolving agent framework that optimizes agent skills and proposes new tools, improving the success rate of an enterprise agentic RAG system grounded in SharePoint content by 5.5 percentage points (81.2% to 86.7%).
Designed `file_evidence`, a Copilot SDK tool that reduced simple file-retrieval latency by 80%.

publications.title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
publications.summary: Led an end-to-end rubric-based evaluation pipeline covering 282 real patient questions, 3,639 clinician-authored rubric criteria, and 22 LLMs. Introduced factuality verification beyond rubric scoring. [Dataset available on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/YiminZ07/PanCanBench).

publications.title: SCOPE: Localizing fate-decision states and their regulatory drivers in single-cell differentiation
publications.publisher: Under major revision at Nature Communications
publications.summary: Developed a framework for localizing cell-fate decision points using semi-supervised learning, graph-based label propagation, and conformal inference. Validated on lineage-tracing and multi-omics datasets containing over 100,000 cells.

publications.title: Agents' Last Exam
publications.publisher: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track
publications.summary: Contributed to a benchmark evaluating agents on long-horizon, economically valuable real-world tasks through verifiable task outcomes.

publications.title: A minimal gene set characterizes multiple classes of tumor-specific TIL among different cancer types
scTIM: seeking cell-type-indicative marker from single cell RNA-seq data by consensus optimization

projects.name: Benchmarking LLMs on Evolving Medical Knowledge
projects.summary: February 2026 - Present. Supervisor: Jeff Leek, Fred Hutch.
highlights: Developed a dynamic benchmark evaluating whether LLMs can resolve conflicts between outdated medical knowledge and newly released authoritative evidence.
Curated evolving and matched static control facts from FDA drug labels, Phase III clinical trials, and clinical guidelines.
Benchmarked LLMs under closed-book, web-search, and oracle-evidence settings to quantify failures in knowledge updating, retrieval, and evidence integration.

projects.name: Beyond Exchangeability: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shifts
projects.summary: March 2026 - Present. Supervisors: Kevin Lin, University of Washington; Mike Wu, Fred Hutch. Paper to be submitted.
highlights: Built a systematic benchmark of eight conformal prediction methods for covariate shift, spanning propensity-score-based, distributionally robust, conditional-guarantee, and covariate-balancing approaches.
Adapted entropy balancing from causal inference to conformal prediction and showed greater robustness than propensity-score-based methods across model specifications and data dimensions.
Examined how the divergence radius in distributionally robust methods trades coverage against interval width.

projects.name: Multi-omics Data Analysis Recommendation with RAG
projects.summary: April 2025 - Present. Supervisor: Mike Wu, Fred Hutch.
highlights: Developed a RAG-based tool for multi-omics analysis recommendation that mitigates hallucinations and delivers concrete, citation-backed guidelines compared with state-of-the-art LLM baselines.
